name: Infants
description: Unhurried, responsive care that follows each baby's own rhythm for feeding, napping, and play.
details: Your baby's day follows their own schedule, not ours. Primary caregivers learn every cue, keep a detailed log of bottles, naps, and diapers, and fill the room with floor time, songs, and sensory play.
image_alt: A caregiver's hands steadying a baby on a soft linen play mat beside wooden toys

name: Toddlers
description: First words, first friends, and plenty of room to climb, pour, stack, and explore.
details: Toddlers learn with their whole bodies. The room is built for climbing, pouring, and stacking, with simple routines — handwashing, snack, clean-up — that build independence one small step at a time.
image_alt: Two toddlers scooping dried beans in a sensory tray at a low wooden table

name: Twos
description: Big feelings, bigger imaginations. Pretend play, early language, and gentle potty learning.
details: Twos are ready for more words, more friends, and more ideas. Pretend play, picture books, and small-group art build language and patience, and potty learning happens gently, in partnership with you.
image_alt: Three-year-olds playing pretend at a wooden play kitchen

name: Preschool & Pre-K
description: Letters, numbers, and questions answered by doing — so kindergarten feels like the next adventure.
details: Project-based learning turns big questions — where do seeds go? why do shadows move? — into weeks of reading, counting, building, and drawing. Pre-K adds kindergarten-readiness work at each child's pace.
image_alt: Pre-K children counting with wooden number tiles at a classroom table
